# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [today's date]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Sawyer Alvarez
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-11
**Member:** Sawyer Alvarez
**Member ID:** W635441117
**Reference number:** POC-A1F3D3C000-86797
**Service denied:** Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Ohio
**Policy I am relying on:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty — https://static.cigna.com/assets/chcp/pdf/coveragePolicies/medical/mm_0285_coveragepositioncriteria_total_ankle_arthroplasty.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), which Cigna denied on 2026-08-11 under reference number POC-A1F3D3C000-86797. The notice states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure.

I am relying on the plan's own published criteria in Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty, named above. Below, I quote the plan's language and then point to what is in my medical records. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed.

---

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Conservative therapy.** The plan's policy states:

> "failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy)"

My records document conservative care in the categories the policy itself names:

- **Anti-inflammatory medications:** I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Physical therapy:** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance — 18 visits over 10 weeks, from 2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- In addition, I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29, which gave me only about two weeks of partial relief.

My symptoms have gone on for 12 months of progressive ankle pain that is not relieved by rest. My trial of anti-inflammatory medication alone ran 8 months — longer than the six months the policy requires — and it failed, as did physical therapy and the injection.

**2. Skeletal maturity.** The policy states:

> "individual is skeletally mature"

I am an adult. My date of birth is [my date of birth], and I ask that Dr. Duval's records be reviewed to confirm this criterion is met.

**3. Effect on daily living and work.** The policy states:

> "interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My records document that I walk with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks, and that my range of motion is limited by pain, with positive provocative testing on the affected side. As to work specifically, my job duties are [my job and the specific duties I can no longer perform], and I am glad to provide anything further the reviewer needs on this point.

**4. Condition in the affected ankle.** The policy states:

> "presence of ONE of the following in the affected ankle:  severe inflammatory arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis)  severe osteoarthritis  post-traumatic arthritis"

My weight-bearing ankle radiographs dated 2026-06-02 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts — that is, the joint space in my ankle is gone. I ask that this imaging, together with Dr. Duval's diagnosis in my chart, be measured against this criterion.

**5. Pain that limits function at short distances.** The policy states:

> "individual has moderate to severe ankle pain that:  is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length "

My records state that I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am **limited to two blocks**. That is the same limitation the plan's own policy gives as its example. I would note that this excerpt of the policy ends mid-sentence in the copy available to me, and the policy appears to list further conditions that are not reproduced there. If Cigna applied any part of this criterion beyond what is quoted above, I ask that it be identified in the appeal response.

**6. Contraindications.** The policy states:

> "individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty:  active infection  insufficient bone/osteonecrosis  loss of musculature in the affected limb/insufficient ligament s"

and

> "Charcot's or other peripheral neuropathy  neurological impairment  severe ankle deformity precluding proper alignment"

My records specifically document **no active infection**. They also document no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. My records do not document any of the other conditions listed above. If Cigna believes one of these contraindications is present in my chart, I ask that the specific finding and the record it comes from be identified.

---

## A note on what I have been able to review

The excerpts I have quoted are the only policy language available to me, and two of them introduce lists that are not fully reproduced in the copy I have. I have not quoted anything beyond that text, and I am not attributing any threshold or requirement to the plan that does not appear in it. Because the denial notice states only that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, without saying which criterion was not met, I am asking Cigna to identify in its response the specific criterion or criteria from Cigna Medical Coverage Policy 0285 Total Ankle Arthroplasty that it found unmet, and the records it reviewed.

---

## What I am requesting

1. That Cigna overturn the denial dated 2026-08-11 (reference POC-A1F3D3C000-86797) and authorize total ankle replacement, CPT 27702.
2. That my appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery.
3. That, if the denial is upheld in whole or in part, Cigna state in writing the exact criterion from the policy above that it found unmet, and the clinical records it relied on.
4. That Cigna provide me, at no charge, a copy of the full policy and any internal clinical guidelines used in this determination.

**Records I am submitting with this appeal:**

- Physical therapy discharge note (18 visits, 2026-04-18 to 2026-06-27)
- Medication records for 8 months of NSAID therapy
- Injection record, 2026-04-29
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report, 2026-06-02
- Office notes and operative recommendation from Dr. Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery
- [Any other records I choose to include]

**Filing and deadline.** My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, by **2027-02-07**. I am submitting this appeal within that window. I am filing it through my.cigna.com, where my plan's appeal form is located, and/or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for my plan. If anything further is needed from me, I can be reached at the phone number above, and I understand I can also call 1-800-244-6224 or the number on my member ID card.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this. I believe my records line up with the plan's own written criteria, and I would like the chance to have that reviewed carefully.

Sincerely,

**Sawyer Alvarez**
Member ID: W635441117
[Signature]
[Date]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
